rule: A complete outfit passes only when the original product images prove season, occasion, silhouette, color balance and modern styling. Final-alpha cutouts cannot overrule contradictory source imagery.

decisions.reason: The source images prove a controlled textured polo, clean tailored green short and low-profile white sneaker. The palette is light, summery and balanced, with no loose-on-loose or skinny proportion.

The washed-blue short-sleeve overshirt has a mottled acid wash, visible chest label and long generic catalog shape. It does not meet the Zara-led quality bar even though the ivory trouser and tan loafer are individually strong.
The white knee-length short uses a dated embossed diagonal texture and conservative synthetic-looking shape. It weakens the otherwise good sage knit and off-white loafer.
A long drop-shoulder T-shirt over an elastic drawstring short creates the loose-on-loose silhouette the user explicitly rejected. The top also lacks on-body fit proof.

The desert-yellow T-shirt source is a long, strongly dropped-shoulder packshot with no on-body fit proof. The tailored short and two-tone loafer are strong, but the complete outfit cannot be approved on an unproved upper silhouette.
The sky-blue one-piece-collar shirt, high-rise pleated khaki trouser and black penny loafer form a controlled modern office silhouette with credible full-product proof.

The orange gauze shirt is the single relaxed element; the clean white straight trouser and two-tone suede loafer control the silhouette. The palette is warm, happy and season-correct for a summer date.
The brown trouser is explicitly sold as slim-fit and the source confirms a narrow cropped ankle. That contradicts the no-skinny menswear direction, regardless of the strong teal-and-taupe palette.

The bright regular-fit fleece, straight technical utility trouser and real trail shoe work as a Fall outdoor-sports look. Keep it limited to trail, hiking or outdoor activity rather than generic gym styling.
